text:
IncBot: INCIDENT RATE_SPIKE_1955553333 detected — sudden 4.8x token/sec increase on streaming generation (region: us-west-2). Paging oncall.
Ava (oncall): seeing alerts. CPU on inference nodes spiking, queue latency rising. Customers reporting 429s and lots of half-open streams.
Jordan (SRE): root metrics: aggregate tokens/sec 4.9x baseline, tail latency (p99) up from 180ms -> 1.7s. Error surface: primarily 429s, plus some transient 503s from worker OOM restarts.
Ava (oncall): can we temporarily shape traffic while we dig in? recommend immediate mitigations: token-rate throttle on streaming endpoints + soft per-customer quota reductions for noisy tenants.
Sam (eng-runtime): agree. I'm going to push a temporary rate-limit policy on edge: limit streaming connections per API key to 6 concurrent, and per-key token/sec cap 60k (from 250k). Applying now.
Sam (eng-runtime): patch command:
```
rctl policy apply --name quick-stream-cap --match endpoint:/v1/stream --concurrency 6 --tokens-per-sec 60000 --duration 15m
```
Jordan (SRE): also enabling emergency prefork restart disable to avoid thrashing: set KEEP_WORKERS_ON_OOM=1 on affected pools.
Maya (platform): I'll prepare a temporary quota update for top 10 token-heavy customers. Using admin API to reduce burst quota by 60% for 30 minutes. Doing batch operation now.
Maya (platform): admin call example:
```
POST /internal/admin/quotas/bulk_adjust
payload: {customers: [...], token_rate_factor: 0.4, duration_minutes: 30}
```
Ava (oncall): Nick — can you craft a short SDK advisory we can post to status and push into the SDKs runtime logs? Need guidance for immediate client-side mitigations.
Nick (dev-advocate): on it. Draft below — feel free to copy into status and release notes.

Nick (dev-advocate): "If you see 429s or aborted streaming responses: implement exponential backoff with jitter, limit concurrent streams, and add idempotency tokens for non-idempotent requests. Recommended client policy:
- base_delay = 300ms
- max_delay = 8s
- max_retries = 5
- jitter: full jitter (random between 0 and backoff)
- on 429: respect Retry-After header when present; otherwise use backoff
- on connection aborts: retry only if request was idempotent OR an idempotency key was provided

JS snippet (pseudo):
```
async function retryWithBackoff(fn) {
  let attempt = 0
  while (attempt < 5) {
    try { return await fn() }
    catch (e) {
      if (!isRetriable(e)) throw e
      const delay = Math.min(8000, 300 * Math.pow(2, attempt))
      await sleep(Math.random() * delay)
      attempt++
    }
  }
  throw new Error('max retries')
}
```
Headers to include for safe retries:
- Idempotency-Key: <uuid>
- X-Client-Request-Type: streaming|sync

Please avoid blind immediate retries for streaming chunks; retry the entire request only when the client can safely re-issue (idempotency key present or operation inherently idempotent)."

Li (customer-success): I'll notify the top impacted customers with the mitigation steps and expected 30-60m window. Include workaround: reduce client concurrency to 2 streams per process and fall back to polling generation for long jobs.
Jordan (SRE): quick check: are there specific model versions spiking? runtime traces show heavy usage of gpt-small-llama variant in the pool 'stream-a'. Might be a runaway loop in a customer app.
Ava (oncall): Sam — can you enable per-model temporary routing to alternate cheaper instances? We can divert new requests to 'safe' pool with lower concurrency.
Sam (eng-runtime): routing change applied: new streaming requests for gpt-small-llama -> pool 'stream-b-safe' (lower throughput, prioritized fairness). Command used:
```
rctl route modify --model gpt-small-llama --to pool:stream-b-safe --duration 20m
```
Maya (platform): also toggled a feature flag to disable function-calling for streaming on rapid-tier customers; reduces token churn. Flag: ff:disable_stream_fncall for tier=rapid.
Ava (oncall): good. We'll monitor 5m. Jordan, keep an eye on worker OOMs.
Jordan (SRE): worker restarts dropped by 60% after throttles. p95 latency falling back toward baseline. Still seeing noisy client at ~3 customers — we should consider targeted temporary API-key throttles and a support outreach.
Li (customer-success): I'm on the outreach for those three. Asking for any evidence of runaway loops or batched retries on their side.
Nick (dev-advocate): addendum to SDK guidance: for streaming clients, recommend an adaptive window: if average token latency > 500ms, reduce token chunk size and increase inter-chunk delay by 200ms; and emit a metric 'client.stream_backoff' to our observability.
Ava (oncall): next: handoff. I'm going offline in 40m. Jordan — can you take the oncall after me? I'll leave steps in the incident doc and escalate if customers don't recover.
Jordan (SRE): I got it. Handoff checklist posted:
- verify rctl policies quick-stream-cap still active
- confirm pool stream-b-safe healthy
- watch top 5 token producers and keep Customer Success looped
- if burst returns, escalate to infra-leads for horizontal scaling or emergency capacity.
Ava (oncall): postmortem action items (quick):
- runtime: add alert for model-specific token surge (Sam)
- platform: add rapid-tier per-key hard cap option (Maya)
- devx: publish SDK sample for idempotency and backoff (Nick)
- support: follow-up with customers about root cause and remediation (Li)

IncBot: Incident RATE_SPIKE_1955553333 status: mitigated -> partial recovery observed. Monitoring for 30m.
Ava (oncall): closing note: if anything regresses ping @Jordan and reopen. I'll create a brief incident timeline in #postmortems once we have the root cause.
Jordan (SRE): acknowledged. taking over monitoring. will update thread with any escalations.
